newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bardot puts heart and soul in memoirs.
newsitem.headline: Bardot puts heart and soul in memoirs.

text.p: Screen goddess turned animal rights activist Brigitte Bardot says she has put her "whole heart, head, soul and guts" in her autobiography due out next month.
"I have gone for the complete truth and absolute sincerity," Bardot, 61, told Paris Match magazine in an interview published on Wednesday.
"I can swear to you that I have put in it my whole heart, head, soul and guts," she said ahead of the publication of "Initiales B.B." on October 1.
Asked about her prosperous family background, her brilliant career, her own wealth and stardom, she answered that her parents had been strict and cinema "did not interest me".
"Every so often, I found happiness, but it didn't last. The overall feeling is of an immense and intense solitude. No one can imagine how much I felt despair and distress," Bardot said.
Once described as France's most famous export, Bardot later turned her back on the sexuality which made her famous and devoted herself to animal welfare.
Bardot made the last of her 42 films in 1973 and, declaring the cinema world to be "rotten," became almost a recluse in the fashionable Riviera resort of Saint-Tropez.
